paper.title: Tight Regret Bounds for Infinite-armed Linear Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Linear contextual bandit with (changing) infinite action sets
unmapped: action sets D_t are closed subsets of the unit l2 ball with |D_t| = infinity, chosen obliviously before the policy runs; D_t revealed at time t
settings.definition_quote: At each time period $t$, an \emph{action set} $D_t\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ is provided; the player selects an \emph{action} $x_t\in D_t$, and subsequently receives a \emph{reward} $r_t = \langle x_t, \theta\rangle + \xi_t$, where $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, $\|\theta\|_2\leq 1$ is a fixed but unknown parameter vector, and $\{\xi_t\}$ are independent centered sub-Gaussian noise variables with the variance proxy 1. ... The domains $D_1,\cdots,D_T\in\mathcal S_d$ are chosen arbitrarily, \emph{before} any policy $\pi$ is executed.

bound.expression_latex: \E\left[\max\left\{R_T - C_1  d \sqrt{ T \log T \log (1/\delta)} \cdot \log \log (T/\delta), 0\right\}\right] \leq C_2 \delta d\sqrt{T}

conditions: D_t closed subsets of the unit l2 ball

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Suppose the universal constant $C>0$ in the input of Algorithm \ref{alg:suplinucb} is sufficiently large. Then there exists constants $C_1, C_2 > 0$ that only depend on $C$ such that for all $\|\theta\|_2\leq 1$ and $\{D_t\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|_2\leq 1\} \}$, the regret $R_T$ satisfies the following inequality {for any $\delta\in(0,1)$}, \E[\max\{R_T - C_1 d \sqrt{ T \log T \log (1/\delta)} \cdot \log \log (T/\delta), 0\}] \leq C_2 \delta d\sqrt{T}.

results.notes: Theorem bounds E[(R_T - C1 d sqrt(T log T log(1/delta)) loglog(T/delta))_+]; recorded as the implied expected regret bound (statement i). With delta = Omega(1) this gives O(d sqrt(T log T) loglog T), matching informal Theorem 1 (O(sqrt(d^2 T log T)) poly(loglog T)). R_T is defined through means, so the expectation is pseudo-regret.

conditions: D_t closed subsets of the unit l2 ball

source.label: thm:main
